text:
maria-support: customer reports intermittent NXDOMAIN for their service endpoint svc.payments.internal after tenant VPC migration. some app pods resolve to the endpoint's private IP, others get public IPs or NXDOMAIN. first seen after cross-account migration yesterday.

maria-support: repro steps from customer: inside pod -> `dig +short svc.payments.internal` returns nothing, `dig svc.payments.internal @10.10.0.2` (VPC resolver) -> NXDOMAIN, but on host `dig +short svc.payments.internal` sometimes returns 10.0.45.12 (private ENI IP).

maria-support: they also ran `curl https://svc.payments.internal/health` from different nodes, some succeed, some time out. suspect split-horizon / hosted zone overlap.

tim-oncall: heya, can you paste outputs of `kubectl exec -it pod -- cat /etc/resolv.conf` and `dig +short @169.254.169.253 svc.payments.internal` from failing pod? also we need `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids` from customer's account?

maria-support: pushed logs, attaching snippets: `resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 169.254.169.253` and `search ns.local svc.cluster.local`. From failing pod `dig @169.254.169.253 svc.payments.internal` -> `;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345`

sre-jun: NXDOMAIN from VPC resolver usually means Route53 private hosted zone answering NXDOMAIN (no record) or resolver rule forwarding wrong. Do they have a private hosted zone for payments.internal in any account? run `aws route53domains list-hosted-zones` and `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name payments.internal`.

maria-support: they ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name payments.internal` in tenant account: no hosted zone. In platform account (where we manage endpoints) there is a private hosted zone payments.internal associated with a different VPC.

kate-eng: aha. Common gotcha: interface VPC endpoints create a Route53 private hosted zone in the endpoint-owner account. If customer created a same-named private hosted zone in their account or in platform account and associated different VPCs, you can get split answers depending on resolver rules and VPC association. Do we see duplicate hosted zones across accounts?

aws-bot: Automated check: private hosted zone payments.internal exists in account A (owner of endpoint) and a separate private hosted zone payments.internal exists in customer account B but has no records. This causes NXDOMAIN when the resolver in VPC resolves against the wrong hosted zone.

maria-support: confirm — customer had manually provisioned a private hosted zone payments.internal during migration, left it empty as placeholder. looks like some VPCs are associated with that empty hosted zone and shadow the endpoint-owned hosted zone.

sre-jun: that matches mixed answers: some nodes' resolver is hitting the endpoint-owner hosted zone (returns ENI IP), others hit the customer's empty hosted zone (NXDOMAIN). Resolution depends on which resolver rule/vpc association and whether node-local cache returns stale answers.

tim-oncall: mitigation steps: 1) remove/rename the empty private hosted zone in the customer account OR 2) disassociate the customer's VPC from the empty hosted zone OR 3) associate the endpoint-owned hosted zone with the customer VPC (if permitted). Recommend customer picks 1 or 2 immediately.

maria-support: customer is nervous to delete zone. requested safe repro and quick check. they asked for a non-destructive way to test impact.

kate-eng: non-destructive check: from a failing node run `dig +short payments.internal @10.10.0.2` then `dig +short payments.internal @10.20.0.2` (resolver IPs for different AZs) and `nslookup payments.internal <resolver-ip>`. Also `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID` to see associated VPCs. If you see the empty hosted zone associated with the VPC, disassociate should fix.

maria-support: pasted `aws route53 get-hosted-zone` for the customer's empty zone: shows VPC association with vpc-0a1b2c3d (their prod VPC). They did not realize AWS allows same-name private zones.

sre-jun: also check node-local-dns or dns cache: `kubectl logs kube-dns -n kube-system` / `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns` — node-local caches can serve stale NXDOMAIN until TTL expires. You might have to `delete` the node-local cache pods to flush.

maria-support: customer confirmed node-local pods were running. flushed by restarting daemonset — some pods immediately started resolving correctly. others still NXDOMAIN.

tim-oncall: for the remaining ones, check VPC resolver rule priority and inbound resolver endpoints if in use. Also check iptables/node egress policies blocking route53 resolver endpoints (TCP/53 or UDP/53). But since some nodes succeed, egress likely fine.

kate-eng: final root cause summary we should send to customer: duplicate private hosted zones with the same domain across accounts caused split-horizon; one hosted zone is empty (NXDOMAIN), shadowing the endpoint-owner hosted zone for some VPC-resolver paths. Replication: create a temporary CNAME in the endpoint-owned hosted zone and query from nodes before/after disassociation to confirm which zone answers.

maria-support: customer accepted disassociation of the empty hosted zone from their VPC during maintenance window. asked for rollback steps.

sre-jun: rollback: re-associate VPC using `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` with the appropriate hosted zone id. If you removed the zone, you'd need to recreate it and re-add records. Note: interface endpoint private hosted zones are managed by endpoint owner — associating wrong zone can re-create the conflict.

maria-support: created ticket with steps and included `dig/nslookup` commands and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone` outputs. customer will disassociate empty zone and monitor.

dns-bot: suggestion: add a runbook entry: "Check for duplicate private hosted zones across accounts when service endpoint resolution is inconsistent" + sample commands.

tim-oncall: marking as escalated->eng-sre if problem persists after disassociation. thx team. :thumbsup:

maria-support: closing loop once customer verifies, will post follow-up here.
